sources.title: President’s biography: birth, engineering, regional posts, premiership and 2016/2021 elections
sources.findings: Read government biography: born 24 July 1957, Zaamin District in Jizzakh; 1981 mechanical-engineering graduation and institute research/teaching/vice-rector work. Mirzo Ulugbek district head in 1992, Jizzakh 1996–2001, Samarkand 2001–2003, premiership from 2003 with confirmations 2005/2010/2015. Parliamentary and executive roles overlap. Temporary presidential powers assigned by joint parliamentary resolution 8 September 2016; election 4 December, formal office 14 December, official share 88.61%. Re-election 24 October 2021 reported as 80.1%, then five-year term. The biography stops detailed election chronology at 2021 despite a 2026 update label; 2023 changes are supplied separately. Promotional praise is not independent impact evidence.

sources.title: Official Russian biography: Candidate of Technical Sciences and academic career
sources.findings: Read official Russian biography alongside English version. Russian explicitly says Candidate of Technical Sciences and docent; English translates the degree as PhD. Profile preserves the original degree designation without inventing an award year, US degree equivalence, higher Doctor of Sciences or current teaching appointment. Mechanical engineering, agricultural irrigation institute and academic administration are distinct from later political offices.

sources.title: 2019 Article IV report, Annex II: exchange-rate unification on 5 September 2017
sources.findings: Read selected Annex II exchange-rate section of IMF 2019 Article IV report, paragraph 15: unification and access liberalization on 5 September 2017, official rate from 4250 to 8100 sum per US dollar. Report also describes remaining capital-flow restrictions and a managed de facto exchange-rate regime. No claim of complete capital-account openness, immediate free floating or a 90% loss in currency value derived incorrectly from the quotation change. Full statistical report and charts were not exhaustively audited.

sources.title: 2021 cotton-harvest monitoring findings, announced 1 March 2022
sources.findings: Read ILO announcement of 1 March 2022 about the 2021 cotton harvest: 11000 picker interviews, 99% voluntary and around 1% direct or perceived coercion. ILO’s systemic-elimination conclusion is retained with these limits. Reported child/adult changes over years and institutional reform are not wholly credited to the president; data do not certify all industries or 2026 conditions. Announcement preceded publication of the full report on 29 March; only announcement findings were read. A separate 29 January 2021 ILO article concerns the 2020 crop and 96% voluntary work and is not conflated with the 2021 harvest.

sources.title: Official results of the 9 July 2023 early presidential election
sources.findings: Read CEC results account for the 9 July 2023 early presidential election: official winner Mirziyoyev with 87.05% of voters participating. Official vote result is attributed to election authorities rather than presented as an independent certification of free competition or share of all residents. Other candidates’ shares are not needed in the profile. ODIHR’s final-report annex reproduces the same result, explicitly according to CEC data.

sources.publisher: OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights
sources.title: 10 July 2023 observation statement: lack of genuine political competition
sources.findings: Read ODIHR’s 10 July 2023 observation statement: technical preparations and some legal reforms acknowledged; genuine competition absent, expression restricted, serious election-day procedural irregularities and integrity concerns observed. None of the registered candidates publicly challenged the incumbent with alternative political views. The profile attributes these judgments to observers, without portraying the official vote share as rebutting them or inventing a criminal verdict.

sources.publisher: OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights
sources.title: Final report on the 9 July 2023 early presidential election
sources.findings: Read selected political-context section and final-results annex of ODIHR final report, notably printed pages 4–5 and 27. April 30 referendum and amended constitution extended presidential term from five to seven years, reset incumbent term count, and empowered early election called 8 May for 9 July. Former term was due to end in 2026; profile does not retain that as the current endpoint. Annex states 13,625,055 votes and 87.05% according to CEC. No full report/observer appendix review is claimed, and a possible future re-election is not treated as guaranteed office until 2037.

sources.title: Presidential inauguration and oath, 14 July 2023
sources.findings: Read actual 14 July 2023 inauguration record: oath at joint parliamentary session after the 9 July election, CEC certificate and seven-year programme. Official assertion of democratic principles is not adopted over independent ODIHR assessment. GDP, investment and green-energy targets in the speech are prospective, not achieved results or personal assets.

sources.title: Completed Muscat talks and strategic partnership with Oman, 17 November 2026
sources.findings: Read presidential press service’s 17 November 2026 account of actual restricted and expanded talks with Sultan Haitham at Al Alam Palace, Muscat. Leaders announced strategic partnership and agreed a roadmap and coordination mechanism. Plans concerning investment capital, funds and projects do not prove money disbursed or construction completed. Dunyo’s same-day account corroborates publication but derives from the presidential press service, so it is not counted as an independent eyewitness source. No original meeting video or signatures were inspected.

sources.title: 2018 Article IV mission statement: foreign-exchange reform and inflation pressures
sources.findings: Read IMF staff concluding statement dated 14 March 2018: September 2017 foreign-exchange liberalization and inflation pressures from exchange-rate/price changes. It is a staff mission statement, not a separate Executive Board decision. The profile does not turn forecasts for 2018–2019 into achieved outcomes or imply that liberalization had no adjustment costs.
